syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: What development promises: different people, different goals
topics.ncert_sections: Different people, different goals

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why persons in different life situations have different developmental goals.
Recognise that what is development for one person may be harmful for another.

topics.title: Income and other goals
topics.ncert_sections: Income and other goals

concepts.learning_objective: Identify non-material goals such as equal treatment, freedom, security and respect alongside income.
Explain that people look at a mix of income and non-income goals when making choices.

topics.title: National development
topics.ncert_sections: National development

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that notions of national development differ and must be judged by fairness and how many people benefit.

topics.title: Comparing countries and states: per capita income and averages
topics.ncert_sections: How to compare different countries or states?; Average income

concepts.learning_objective: Define per capita income and explain why it is used to compare countries.
State the World Bank's criterion for classifying countries.
Calculate averages and explain why they can hide disparities in distribution.

topics.title: Income and other criteria; public facilities
topics.ncert_sections: Income and other criteria; Public facilities

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret infant mortality rate, literacy rate and net attendance ratio to compare states.
Explain why collective provision of health, education and PDS improves well-being.

topics.title: Human Development Report
topics.ncert_sections: Human Development Report

concepts.learning_objective: State the criteria the UNDP's Human Development Report uses to compare countries.
Interpret Human Development Report data comparing India with its neighbours.

topics.title: Sustainability of development
topics.ncert_sections: Sustainability of development

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources with examples such as groundwater and crude oil.
Explain why development must be sustainable for future generations.

topics.title: Sectors of economic activities
topics.ncert_sections: Sectors of Economic Activities

concepts.learning_objective: Classify economic activities into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors by the nature of the activity.
Explain how the three sectors depend on one another using everyday examples.

topics.title: Comparing the three sectors: GDP and historical change
topics.ncert_sections: Comparing the Three Sectors; Historical Change in Sectors

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish final goods from intermediate goods and explain why only final goods are counted.
Define GDP and calculate the value of production while avoiding double counting.
Describe how the most important sector changed over time in now developed countries.

topics.title: Primary, secondary and tertiary sectors in India
topics.ncert_sections: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Sectors in India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the reasons for the rising importance of the tertiary sector in India's production.
Analyse why employment did not shift out of the primary sector as production did.
Explain underemployment or disguised unemployment with rural and urban examples.

topics.title: How to create more employment
topics.ncert_sections: How to Create More Employment?

concepts.learning_objective: Suggest ways of creating employment through irrigation, credit, agro-based industry and services.
Describe the provisions and purpose of MGNREGA 2005 as the Right to Work.

topics.title: Organised and unorganised sectors
topics.ncert_sections: Division of Sectors as Organised and Unorganised; How to Protect Workers in the Unorganised Sector?

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the organised and unorganised sectors on the basis of employment conditions.
Identify vulnerable workers in the unorganised sector and explain why they need protection.

topics.title: Sectors in terms of ownership: public and private
topics.ncert_sections: Sectors in Terms of Ownership: Public and Private Sectors

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between public and private sectors on the basis of ownership and motive.
Explain why the government undertakes or supports certain economic activities.

topics.title: Money as a Medium of Exchange

concepts.learning_objective: Explain double coincidence of wants as the essential feature, and difficulty, of a barter system.
Explain how money acts as an intermediate in exchange and removes the need for double coincidence of wants.
Explain why modern currency, though of no use in itself, is accepted as a medium of exchange in India.
Explain demand deposits and how cheque payments against them settle transactions without cash.
Describe how banks use deposits to give loans and mediate between depositors and borrowers.
Explain why banks hold only a small share of deposits as cash and how they earn their main income.
Define credit and explain how it helps meet the working capital needs of production.
Analyse how risk and the absence of support in case of loss can push a borrower into a debt trap.
Define collateral and explain why lenders ask for it.
Identify the components of terms of credit and compare credit arrangements using them.
Compare the sources and terms of credit available to different people in a village.
Describe how cooperative societies raise funds and provide loans to their members.
Distinguish formal from informal sources of credit and explain the effects of high-cost informal credit.
Describe how the Reserve Bank of India supervises the functioning of formal lenders.
Analyse why richer households get a larger share of formal credit than poorer households.
Explain how Self Help Groups work and how they help the poor overcome the lack of collateral.
Describe the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh as an example of reaching the poor with credit.

topics.title: Production across countries and MNCs
topics.ncert_sections: Production across countries

concepts.learning_objective: Define a multinational corporation (MNC) and distinguish it from a company that only trades abroad.
Explain why and how MNCs divide production into parts and spread it across countries.

topics.title: Interlinking production across countries
topics.ncert_sections: Interlinking production across countries

concepts.learning_objective: Explain investment and foreign investment with examples such as Ford Motors and Cargill Foods.
Describe the ways in which MNCs set up, control or influence production in other countries.

topics.title: Foreign trade and integration of markets
topics.ncert_sections: Foreign trade and integration of markets

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how foreign trade lets producers reach beyond domestic markets and widens buyers' choice.
Explain how foreign trade connects markets, equalises prices and increases competition between countries.

topics.title: What is globalisation?
topics.ncert_sections: What is globalisation?

concepts.learning_objective: Define globalisation as rapid integration of countries through foreign trade and foreign investment.
Identify the movements of goods, services, investments, technology and people that link countries.

topics.title: Technology as a factor enabling globalisation
topics.ncert_sections: Factors that have enabled globalisation: Technology

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how improvements in transportation technology have stimulated globalisation.
Explain the role of information and communication technology in spreading production of services.

topics.title: Liberalisation, the WTO and steps to attract foreign investment
topics.ncert_sections: Liberalisation of foreign trade and foreign investment policy; World Trade Organisation; Steps to attract foreign investment

concepts.learning_objective: Explain trade barriers such as import taxes and quotas, and the meaning and reasons for liberalisation in India.
Describe the aims of the WTO and evaluate the fairness of its rules for developing countries.
Describe SEZs and flexible labour laws as steps taken to attract foreign investment.

topics.title: Impact of globalisation in India and the struggle for a fair globalisation
topics.ncert_sections: Impact of globalisation in India; The struggle for a fair globalisation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the groups and companies in India that have benefited from globalisation.
Explain how rising competition has affected small producers and workers.
Explain what fair globalisation means and the role of government and people in achieving it.
Identify the ways in which consumers are exploited in the marketplace, such as under-weighing, hidden charges and adulterated or defective goods.
Explain why markets are unfair when a few powerful producers face scattered consumers, and why rules are needed to protect consumers.
Trace how the consumer movement in India arose as a social force in the 1960s and changed who is held responsible for quality.
Describe the role of the 1985 UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection and of Consumers International.
Recall the enactment of the Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) in 1986 and its amendment in 2019.

topics.title: Right to safety and right to be informed

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the right to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life and property.
Explain why manufacturers must display particulars such as ingredients, expiry date and MRP on goods.
Describe how the Right to Information Act, 2005 lets citizens obtain information about the functioning of government departments.

topics.title: Right to choice and right to seek redressal

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise situations in which a consumer's right to choose is denied, such as forced tie-in purchases.
Explain the right to seek redressal and compensation against unfair trade practices and exploitation.
Describe how a consumer, individually or as a group, can file and conduct a complaint before a Consumer Commission.

topics.title: Consumer protection councils and the three-tier redressal machinery

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the role of voluntary consumer protection councils and Residents' Welfare Associations in helping consumers.
Identify the district, state and national Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions and the value of claims each one handles.
Interpret quality marks such as ISI, Agmark, Hallmark and +F, and when certification is mandatory.
Describe how the government spreads consumer awareness, including Departments of Consumer Affairs and National Consumers' Day.
Evaluate the progress made by the consumer movement in India and the role of consumers' active involvement.
Explain why the consumer redressal process has become cumbersome, expensive and time consuming.
State the changes brought in by the 2019 amendment of COPRA, such as online purchases and mediation.
